trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out left, right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Going up would leave both cell (1,1) and number 5 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
I can't rule out right or through the portal to (1,5) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going down would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So my guess (right from cell (3,2)) was wrong, so the line must go through the portal to (1,5).
Going left would force the line onto number 5 before its turn; going down would strand number 2: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
I can't rule out down or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Going left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4). So the line goes down.
Number 3 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going down would wall in number 9, the last number; going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up.
Going through the portal to (2,1) would leave both cell (1,1) and number 6 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Cell (2,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.

Going down would cut off the bottom-right corner (3 cells). So the line goes left.
Cell (5,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
